description:
Follow-up to cross-surface-known-divergence-baseline-hygiene (PR #903, DONE). The
default-FAIL half (a known divergence that no longer reproduces fails the gate
instead of silently passing) landed correctly. But the YAML also promised a
maintenance affordance — a flag/Make target to drop a resolved baseline entry —
and that was NOT built: removing a resolved known-divergence entry from the
baseline is fully manual. Makefile was in the item's only_modify list but is
untouched in the #903 diff. Manual baseline pruning is exactly the toil that lets
baselines rot, so this completes the promised affordance.

COMPLETED via #935 (merged 2026-07-05). Shipped as a YAML data-file baseline
(benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface_baseline.yaml) loaded and pruned by
benchbox/core/equivalence/known_divergences_baseline.py, plus the
`cross-surface-update-baseline` Make target and golden tests -- NOT the in-source
AST rewrite the original prior_art assumed (that first cut was redesigned in review).
The writer lives under core/equivalence/, not benchbox/cli/ as scope_limit listed,
to satisfy the utils<core<platforms<cli import layering enforced by #952's lint-imports.

anti_patterns.dont: auto-prune the baseline as a side effect of the normal gate run
reformat or reorder surviving baseline entries

deferrals.reason: Out of scope; this item only provides the manual affordance. Automation is a separate hygiene item.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] duplicate: Exact match: open item is literally 'auto-detect and PR resolved cross-surface baseline entries on a schedule'. (tracked by cross-surface-baseline-stale-entry-autodetect)
deferrals.summary: Auto-detect-and-PR stale baseline entries on a schedule.

preserves.behavior: A still-reproducing divergence is never removed; only entries that no longer diverge are dropped.
The default gate behavior is unchanged: --update-baseline is an explicit opt-in writer, never invoked by the blocking gate run.

prior_art.concept: {'ref': 'Makefile', 'note': 'Existing cross-surface gate Make targets (correctness-gate region); add cross-surface-update-baseline next to them, matching their uv run invocation style.'}

{'ref': 'benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py:1421', 'note': 'The known-divergence baseline read/emit path from #903; the --update-baseline writer goes here, reusing the existing baseline file format and loader.'}

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/equivalence/ -k update_baseline -q
verifications.description: Update-baseline drops only resolved entries and is idempotent
verifications.expected: stale entry removed, live entry preserved, second run no-op

work_units.notes:
grep Makefile for update-baseline (expect: absent) and locate the current
known-divergence baseline read/emit site in cross_surface.py (line numbers in
this TODO are origin/develop at review time and drift). Record the live
file:line in the PR body before editing.
work_units.summary: Re-confirm on fresh develop that no --update-baseline affordance exists and locate the live baseline path

work_units.notes:
Implement the writer that rewrites the baseline file removing entries that no
longer reproduce a divergence, preserving every still-live entry and the file's
existing ordering/format. Must be a no-op (idempotent) on a second run when no
entries changed. Reuse the #903 loader; do not fork the format.
work_units.summary: Add --update-baseline to the cross-surface gate CLI that drops only no-longer-diverging entries

work_units.notes:
Wire a Makefile target invoking the flag, placed beside the existing
correctness-gate / cross-surface targets and following their style.

Seed a baseline with one stale (now-resolved) and one live divergence; run
--update-baseline; assert only the stale entry is removed and the live one is
byte-preserved; assert a second run is a no-op. Mark fast.
work_units.summary: Golden test: stale entry dropped, live entry preserved, second run idempotent
